nodes.summary: Impartial Tak is the placement game on the $n \times n$ board whose play ends once the tokens contain a road. Let $n \ge 4$ and let $x$ be a natural number with $n^2 - 4(n - 2) - 2 \le x \le n^2 - 2n$. Then there is an Impartial Tak penult on the $n \times n$ board with exactly $x$ tokens.
nodes.title: Impartial Tak penults of every size from $n^2 - 4(n - 2) - 2$ to $n^2 - 2n$

nodes.summary: Impartial Tak is the placement game on the $n \times n$ board whose play ends once the tokens contain a road. For every $n \ge 6$ there is an Impartial Tak penult $S$ on the $n \times n$ board whose number of tokens $|S|$ satisfies $3|S| + 8 = n^2 + 4n$ if $n \equiv 1$ or $4 \pmod 6$, $3|S| + 12 = n^2 + 4n$ if $n \equiv 2$ or $3 \pmod 6$, $3|S| + 16 = n^2 + 6n$ if $n \equiv 5 \pmod 6$, and $3|S| + 18 = n^2 + 6n$ if…
nodes.title: Impartial Tak penults with about $n^2/3$ tokens

nodes.summary: Impartial Tak is the impartial placement game on the $n \times n$ board in which the players alternately place a token on an empty cell, play ends once the tokens contain a road, and the player unable to move loses. On the $5 \times 5$ board the first player wins from the empty board.
nodes.title: The first player wins Impartial Tak on the $5 \times 5$ board

nodes.summary: Impartial Tak is the placement game on the $n \times n$ board whose play ends once the tokens contain a road. For every $n \ge 2$, the largest number of tokens in an Impartial Tak penult on the $n \times n$ board is $U(n) = n^2 - 2n$: some penult has exactly $n^2 - 2n$ tokens and no penult has more.
nodes.title: The largest Impartial Tak penult

nodes.summary: Impartial Tak is the impartial placement game on the $n \times n$ board in which the players alternately place a token on an empty cell, play ends once the tokens contain a road, and the player unable to move loses. If $n$ is even, the first player does not win from the empty $n \times n$ board, that is, the second player wins.
nodes.title: The second player wins Impartial Tak on even boards

nodes.summary: Impartial Tak is the placement game on the $n \times n$ board whose play ends once the tokens contain a road. There is a real constant $C$ such that for every natural number $n$, every Impartial Tak penult on the $n \times n$ board has at least $n^2/5 - Cn$ tokens; that is, every penult has at least $n^2/5 + O(n)$ tokens.
nodes.title: An $n^2/5$ lower bound for Impartial Tak penults

nodes.summary: Impartial Tak is the placement game on the $n \times n$ board whose play ends once the tokens contain a road. There is a real constant $C$ such that for every natural number $n$, every Impartial Tak penult on the $n \times n$ board has at least $n^2/4 - Cn$ tokens; that is, every penult has at least $n^2/4 + O(n)$ tokens.
nodes.title: An $n^2/4$ lower bound for Impartial Tak penults

nodes.summary: Impartial Tak is the placement game on the $n \times n$ board whose play ends once the tokens contain a road. For every $n \ge 5$, every Impartial Tak penult $S$ on the $n \times n$ board satisfies $7(n - 4)^2 \le 26|S|$, that is, it has at least $\frac{7}{26}(n - 4)^2$ tokens.
nodes.title: A $\frac{7}{26}(n - 4)^2$ lower bound for Impartial Tak penults

nodes.summary: Impartial Tak is the placement game on the $n \times n$ board whose play ends once the tokens contain a road. Let $S$ be an Impartial Tak penult on the $n \times n$ board and let $c$ be an interior cell, that is, a cell in neither the first nor the last row and in neither the first nor the last column. Then $S$ contains $c$ or a cell orthogonally adjacent to $c$: every Cross (an interior cell together with its four…
nodes.title: Every Cross meets an Impartial Tak penult

nodes.summary: Impartial Tak is the placement game on the $n \times n$ board whose play ends once the tokens contain a road. Index the rows and columns by $0, \dots, n - 1$, let $S$ be an Impartial Tak penult on the $n \times n$ board, and let $r, c$ be natural numbers with $r + 4 \le n$ and $c + 4 \le n$. The Thick Cross at $(r, c)$ is the $4 \times 4$ window of cells in rows $r, \dots, r + 3$ and columns $c, \dots, c + 3$ with…
nodes.title: Every Thick Cross holds three tokens of an Impartial Tak penult

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a penult of Impartial Tak on the $n \times n$ board, with rows and columns numbered from $0$. For all natural numbers $r, c$ with $r + 5 \le n$ and $c + 5 \le n$, consider the $5 \times 5$ window of rows $r, \dots, r + 4$ and columns $c, \dots, c + 4$, and give each token of $S$ in the window, lying in row $i$ and column $j$ of the board, the Weighted Cross weight of position $(i - r, j - c)$. Then the…
nodes.title: Weighted Cross bound for Impartial Tak penults

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a penult of Impartial Tic on the $4 \times 4$ board, then at most $9$ cells of the board lie outside $S$.
nodes.title: Dual Impartial Tic penults on the 4 × 4 board have at most 9 tokens

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 5$. If $S$ is a penult of Impartial Tic on the $n \times n$ board, then at most $4(n - 2)$ cells of the board lie outside $S$.
nodes.title: Token bound for dual Impartial Tic penults

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 5$ and let $x$ be a natural number with $2n \le x \le 4(n - 2)$. Then there is a penult $S$ of Impartial Tic on the $n \times n$ board such that exactly $x$ cells of the board lie outside $S$.
nodes.title: Token counts of dual Impartial Tic penults

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, under normal play the first player wins Impartial Tic on the $n \times n$ board, starting from the empty board, if and only if $n$ is odd; for even $n$ the second player wins.
nodes.title: The first player wins Impartial Tic exactly on odd boards

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set of cells and $E$ a predicate on subsets of $\alpha$ saying when play has ended. In the placement game on $\alpha$ with end predicate $E$, a position $T$ is a move from a position $S$ if and only if $E(S)$ fails and $T = S \cup \{c\}$ for some cell $c \notin S$.
nodes.title: Moves of a placement game

nodes.summary: For every $n$, the empty $n \times n$ board contains no road of Impartial Tak.
nodes.title: The empty board has no Tak road

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 1$, play of Impartial Tic has not ended on the empty $n \times n$ board: no row and no column is full.
nodes.title: Impartial Tic has not ended on the empty board

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set of cells and $E$ a predicate on subsets of $\alpha$ saying when play has ended. In the placement game on $\alpha$ with end predicate $E$, the player to move from a position $S \subseteq \alpha$ wins if and only if $E(S)$ fails and there is a cell $c \notin S$ such that the player to move from $S \cup \{c\}$ does not win.
nodes.title: Normal-play recursion for placement games

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set of cells and $E$ a predicate on subsets of $\alpha$ saying when play has ended. The player to move from a position $S \subseteq \alpha$ wins the placement game on $\alpha$ with end predicate $E$ when $S$ is not a P-position of that game under normal play, in which the player unable to move loses.
nodes.title: First-player win in a placement game

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set of cells and let $E$ be a predicate on subsets of $\alpha$, the condition under which play has ended. The placement game is the impartial game whose positions are the subsets $S \subseteq \alpha$ (the occupied cells), starting from the empty board $\emptyset$. If $E(S)$ holds there are no moves from $S$; otherwise the moves from $S$ lead to the positions $S \cup \{c\}$ with…
nodes.title: The placement game

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set of cells and let $E$ be a predicate on subsets of $\alpha$, the condition under which play has ended. A position $S \subseteq \alpha$ is a penult when it is not terminal and all of its options are ults: $S$ is not terminal, and $S \cup \{c\}$ is an ult for every cell $c \notin S$.
nodes.title: Penults of a placement game

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set of cells. For every predicate $E$ on subsets of $\alpha$, the full board $\alpha$ is a terminal position of the placement game with ending condition $E$.
nodes.title: The full board is terminal

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set of cells and let $E$ be a predicate on subsets of $\alpha$, the condition under which play has ended. A position $S \subseteq \alpha$ (the set of occupied cells) is terminal when $E(S)$ holds or $S = \alpha$: play has ended, or every cell is occupied. These are the positions with no options.
nodes.title: Terminal positions of a placement game

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite set of cells and let $E$ be a predicate on subsets of $\alpha$, the condition under which play has ended. A position $S \subseteq \alpha$ is an ult when it is not terminal but has a terminal option: $S$ is not terminal, and there is a cell $c \notin S$ such that $S \cup \{c\}$ is terminal.
nodes.title: Ults of a placement game

nodes.summary: The weights $w(a, b)$ of the Weighted Cross over the $5 \times 5$ window sum to $26$: $\sum_{a=0}^{4} \sum_{b=0}^{4} w(a, b) = 26$.
nodes.title: Total weight of the Weighted Cross

nodes.summary: Two cells $p = (p_1, p_2)$ and $q = (q_1, q_2)$ of the $n \times n$ board $\{0, \dots, n-1\}^2$, written as (row, column), are orthogonally adjacent when they lie in the same row and their columns differ by $1$ ($p_1 = q_1$ and $|p_2 - q_2| = 1$), or they lie in the same column and their rows differ by $1$ ($p_2 = q_2$ and $|p_1 - q_1| = 1$).
nodes.title: Orthogonal adjacency

nodes.summary: Write the cells of the $n \times n$ board as pairs (row, column) in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}^2$. Impartial Tak has ended at a set $S$ of occupied cells when the tokens contain an orthogonal path from an edge of the board to the opposite edge: there are a token $a \in S$ and a cell $b$ joined by a sequence $a = p_0, p_1, \dots, p_k = b$ with $k \ge 0$, in which each $p_{i+1}$ is a token in $S$ orthogonally adjacent to…
nodes.title: Roads in Impartial Tak

nodes.summary: Write the cells of the $n \times n$ board as pairs $(r, c)$ (row, column) in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}^2$. Impartial Tic has ended at a set $S$ of occupied cells when some row or some column is full: there is a row $r$ with $(r, c) \in S$ for every column $c$, or there is a column $c$ with $(r, c) \in S$ for every row $r$.
nodes.title: End of Impartial Tic

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the weight $w(a, b)$ is $0$ if $a, b \in \{0, 4\}$; otherwise it is $2$ if $a = 2$ and $1 \le b \le 3$, or $b = 2$ and $1 \le a \le 3$; and it is $1$ in all other cases. On the $5 \times 5$ window $0 \le a, b \le 4$ this puts weight $0$ at the four corners, $2$ on the central plus (the centre $(2, 2)$ and its four orthogonal neighbours) and $1$ elsewhere.
nodes.title: Weights of the Weighted Cross

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
